drafts.label: Reply · workday without the box (values jab)
drafts.body:
Two years without ChatGPT felt normal. Now a workday without it can feel impossible.

That's how fast cognitive offload becomes identity.

Useful tools. Real risk: forgetting you used to finish the day with your own brain still in the chair.
drafts.why: Grounded in couple-years ChatGPT + cognitive labour offload + can't imagine workday without it.
drafts.tip: Only main-post claims; do not invent study stats or student essay details from thread replies.

quality.notes: Two-years hook mirrors source pace; identity offload; human chair line without Alzheimer's-style invent.

drafts.label: Reply · prove-a-point pricing ends (blunt systems)
drafts.body:
Prove-a-point API pricing works until demand shows up.

When the cheapest near-frontier lane gets "significantly" more expensive, open weights and self-host stop looking like hobbies.

Access isn't the launch sticker. It's what still lets a builder practice after the bargain ends.
drafts.why: Grounded in significant price rise + cheapest near-frontier + demand broke prove-a-point rates + open-weight/Ollama demand context.
drafts.tip: Avoid stacking unverified competitor model names; stay on pricing/demand/access.

quality.notes: Prove-a-point hook from source; significantly quoted; access = post-bargain practice without sludge unlock.

drafts.label: Short · free tool still needs a room
drafts.body:
A free model on a phone still fails if a student never gets a quiet hour and one human who asks, "Show me how you thought."

Access is necessary. It isn't sufficient.

The room around the tool is half the education — and that's the part we keep skipping because it's harder to ship.
drafts.why: Independent accessibility pillar — tool + room + human; zero mashup of workday offload identity or API prove-a-point pricing.

quality.notes: Independent insight: access without quiet hour + human 'show me how you thought' is incomplete education. Bookmark/RT for teachers; soul + spine; not pack collage.
